---
title: "Markdown"
---

chameleon-rs can convert Markdown to HTML while it renders, with a `markdown:` expression:

```html
<article>${markdown: episode.notes}</article>
<div tal:content="markdown: comment.text"></div>
```

It's opt-in: Chameleon has nothing like it, so you turn it on with `configure()` and use it in
new templates. The converter is built into chameleon-rs (comrak, in Rust), so there's no
Markdown package to install.

## Turn it on

```{python}
import chameleon_rs
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate

chameleon_rs.configure(markdown=True)

page = PageTemplate('<article>${markdown: notes}</article>')
print(page(notes='# Show notes\n\nWe talked about **templates** and `Rust`.'))
```

`configure(markdown=True)` registers the `markdown:` prefix with the defaults. Call it once at
startup, before your templates compile: a template takes the Markdown settings in effect when
it's compiled.

## What it supports

[CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/) plus the GitHub extensions: tables, strikethrough, task
lists, autolinks for bare URLs, and footnotes.

```{python}
notes = """\
| Engine | Speed |
|---|---|
| chameleon-rs | ~~slow~~ fast |

- [x] Ship it, see https://example.com
"""
print(page(notes=notes))
```

Fenced code blocks get a `language-…` class, so a client-side highlighter such as highlight.js
or Prism can color them:

```{python}
print(page(notes='```python\nprint("hi")\n```'))
```

## Values

- The text after `markdown:` is an ordinary expression, so a `|` fallback works:
  `markdown: episode.notes | 'No notes yet.'`. As everywhere in TALES, the fallback is used when
  the expression raises (a missing attribute, say), not when its value is `None`.
- `None` and `''` render nothing. Any other non-string value is converted with `str()` first.
- `default` works as for any expression: `tal:content="markdown: page.notes | default"` keeps
  the element's own content when `page.notes` is missing.
- The result is markup, like `structure:`, so it isn't escaped again.

```{python}
print(PageTemplate('<div>${markdown: missing.notes | "*Coming soon*"}</div>')())
print(PageTemplate('<p>[${markdown: notes}]</p>')(notes=None))
```

## Safe by default

Raw HTML in the Markdown is shown as text, not passed through. That's the right default for
text you don't fully control, such as user comments:

```{python}
print(page(notes='Nice post! <script>alert("hi")</script>'))
```

Links with a `javascript:`, `vbscript:`, `file:` or `data:` URL (other than an image) lose the URL too.

For content you trust, such as your own articles, allow raw HTML in a separate profile (see
below). `raw_html: 'allow'` lets those URLs through as well.

"Safe" here is about markup and requests, not CPU time. Some inputs are slow to convert: a
table with thousands of columns can take seconds. If anyone can post the text, limit its
length when you accept it, and consider turning tables off for that profile
(`'extensions': {'table': False}`).

## Profiles: one prefix per kind of content

Different content needs different settings: your own articles may allow HTML, while comments
shouldn't even load images. Each profile is its own expression prefix:

```{python}
chameleon_rs.configure(markdown={
    'markdown': {},                                     # the defaults
    'md-trusted': {'raw_html': 'allow', 'heading_ids': True},
    'md-comment': {'images': False},
    'md-inline': {'inline': True},
})

page = PageTemplate("""\
<h1>${md-inline: post.title}</h1>
<article>${md-trusted: post.body}</article>
<div tal:repeat="c post.comments">${md-comment: c}</div>
""")


class Post:
    title = 'Hello *world*'
    body = '## Intro\n\nSome <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr>.'
    comments = ['Look: ![tracker](https://example.com/pixel.png)']


print(page(post=Post()))
```

A profile name is a prefix, so it uses lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, and can't be
one of Chameleon's own (`python`, `string`, `structure`, ...). A template class that defines a
prefix itself in `expression_types` keeps its own.

### Profile options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `raw_html` | `'escape'` | `'escape'` shows raw HTML as text. `'allow'` passes it through: trusted content only. |
| `images` | `True` | `False` renders an image as its alt text, so the text can't make the page load a remote image. |
| `inline` | `False` | Drops the `<p>` around output that's a single paragraph, for titles and one-liners. |
| `heading_ids` | `False` | `True` gives headings GitHub-style ids and anchor links. A string adds a prefix to each id, such as `'doc-'` (letters, digits, `-` and `_`). |
| `classes` | `{}` | A class attribute per element, such as `{'table': 'table is-striped', 'pre': 'code'}`. Elements: `p`, `h1`–`h6`, `blockquote`, `ul`, `ol`, `li`, `pre`, `code`, `table`, `a`, `img`, `hr`. See the notes below. |
| `extensions` | all on | Switch GFM extensions off: `{'table': False}`. Keys: `table`, `strikethrough`, `tasklist`, `autolink`, `footnotes`. |

```{python}
chameleon_rs.configure(markdown={'markdown': {'classes': {'table': 'table is-striped', 'blockquote': 'note'}}})
print(PageTemplate('${markdown: s}')(s='> Tip\n\n| a |\n|---|\n| 1 |'))
```

Notes on `classes`:

- Only elements the Markdown produces get a class. Raw HTML in the text never does.
- `code` is inline code. A fenced block's `<code>` keeps its `language-…` class; style it
  through `pre`.
- The footnote list, footnote references and back-links, and heading anchor links don't get
  the `ol`, `li` and `a` classes. Footnote paragraphs do get the `p` class.
- A paragraph inside a tight list (no blank lines between items) has no `<p>` tag, so it gets
  no `p` class.

Each conversion numbers its heading ids on its own, so two `markdown:` blocks with
`heading_ids` on one page can repeat an id. Give each block a profile with its own prefix.

A bad setting raises `ValueError` (or `TypeError` for a value of the wrong type) when you call
`configure()`, and changes nothing.

## Speed and the cache

The converter is fast: a 5 KB document with tables, lists, code and footnotes converts in
about 55 µs, about 26x faster than mistune with the same extensions.

On top of that, chameleon-rs keeps recent conversions in a cache shared by all threads: the
same text with the same profile isn't converted twice. A cache hit costs about 0.3 µs for a
5 KB document. The cache holds 1,024 conversions by default, and at most 64 MB of text and
HTML whatever the count. Texts over 64 KB are converted every time rather than cached:

```python
chameleon_rs.configure(markdown_cache=4096)   # entries; 0 turns the cache off
```

Changing the Markdown settings empties the cache.

## Async renders

`render_async` works with `markdown:`, with one rule shared by every expression type: only an
expression's final value is awaited, not a value inside it. Load the Markdown text in your
view before rendering, rather than passing a coroutine for `markdown:` to convert.
